items.details:

items.title: Fix the source sampling in ScaleRotateShape(), then step the coordinates incrementally
items.details:
`ra/assets/shape_draw.cc`.

The destination-to-source mapping has three defects, visible on an 8x6 test shape at a half turn, at west, and at north with scale 0x180:

- It maps each destination pixel's corner (`x - width`), not its centre, so the result sits one pixel off the centre of the doubled frame.
- `static_cast<int>` truncates toward zero, so source coordinates in (-1, 1) all become 0: the first source row and column are drawn one pixel too wide (13 columns where 12 are right at scale 1.5).
- At quarter turns `std::cos`/`std::sin` return about 1e-16 instead of 0, so coordinates that should be exact integers fall on either side of a pixel boundary and rows come out spliced or duplicated.

Fix: sample the pixel centre (`x + 0.5 - width`, `y + 0.5 - height`), take `floor`, and use exact matrix entries (0, +-1) when the angle is a multiple of 64. Expected results: a half turn of an 8x6 shape is the source reversed in columns 4..11, rows 3..8; north at scale 1.5 is 12x9 in columns 2..13, rows 1..9 with every source pixel 1 or 2 wide. Add golden unit tests for these (the function has none); it changes how every rotated or scaled shape draws, usually by a one-pixel shift, so re-record the `tools/ui_check.py` screenshots that change.

Then step the source coordinates per x (start computed once per row, a constant added per pixel) instead of four multiplies per pixel. Measured 2026-10-05 on the current mapping: 11.3 -> 8.0 us per 48x48 shape, but 5,503 of 10,240 rotation/scale/size cases moved pixels, 90% of them at quarter turns, because the accumulated rounding crosses the same exact boundaries. With centre sampling only 175 cases differ (odd-sized shapes at quarter turns, where a half-pixel centre still lands on a boundary); keep the stepping only if the golden tests and a sweep of all 256 rotations show it reproduces the corrected output exactly, e.g. by using the exact integer path for quarter turns. `std::floor` is a libm call without SSE4.1 and cost more than the stepping saved (30 vs 11 us), so floor with integer arithmetic or an offset that keeps the value positive.

items.title: Decide how a team type entry's counts above 255 or below 0 are read
items.details:
`TeamType::ReadIniEntry()` (`ra/ai/team_type.cc`) casts the initial number and the maximum number of teams to the `unsigned char` the team type stores (it is in the saved game, so the type stays): a scenario's 999 is read as 231 and 256 as 0, which means the team is never created (`CreateTeam()` compares `team_count_ < max_teams_`). `2d9b4f60` clamped the same two fields in the editor dialog to 0..255.

To decide: above 255 should clearly clamp to 255, but -1 wraps to 255 today, effectively "no limit", and a plain `std::clamp(value, 0, 255)` would turn it into 0, never created. Either clamp and keep the wrap for negatives, or clamp both ends knowingly. A `set_max_teams(int)` / `set_initial_count(int)` pair on `TeamType` would then own the conversion for the reader and the dialog (about 15 lines plus tests). Run `30c6f6ae..e9ac6245`.
